title: What do Good Laboratory Practice rules require for laboratory personnel training and records?
description: What the OECD Principles of GLP and FDA's 21 CFR Part 58 require for nonclinical study staff training, records and retention, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) rules require everyone conducting or supervising a nonclinical safety study to have the education, training and experience for their assigned functions, and require the test facility to keep a current record of each person's training, experience and job description. The OECD Principles of GLP, applied in the EU through Directive 2004/10/EC, and the US Food and Drug Administration's 21 CFR Part 58 both make test facility management responsible and require the records to be archived.
keyTakeaways: 21 CFR 58.29(b) requires a current summary of training and experience and a job description for each individual engaged in or supervising a nonclinical laboratory study.

The OECD Principles (section II.1.1) require management to keep a record of qualifications, training, experience and job description for each professional and technical individual, and to provide training where necessary.

Study personnel must be knowledgeable in the parts of GLP that apply to their involvement in the study (OECD II.1.4), and management must assure that personnel clearly understand their functions (21 CFR 58.31(f)).

Training records are archived study records: under 21 CFR 58.195 they follow the study retention periods, and the OECD Principles list them among materials retained for the period set by the authorities.
FDA proposed in August 2016 to add explicit GLP and species-specific training requirements to 58.29. As at November 2026 no final rule has been published and the codified text is unchanged.
jurisdiction: International standards (OECD Principles of GLP), with United States (federal) and European Union implementation
regulator: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) for the Principles of GLP; US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for 21 CFR Part 58; EU Member State GLP monitoring authorities under Directive 2004/10/EC
appliesTo: Test facilities and test sites conducting nonclinical health and environmental safety studies intended for regulatory submission
Test facility management, study directors and principal investigators
All study personnel, including technical and animal care staff

sections.heading: What are GLP rules and which studies do they cover?

blocks.text: GLP is a quality system for nonclinical safety studies whose data are submitted to regulators, and it sets explicit personnel and record requirements. Internationally, the reference text is the OECD Principles of Good Laboratory Practice. In the EU, [Directive 2004/10/EC](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32004L0010) requires Member States to ensure that laboratories testing chemical products comply with the GLP principles reproduced in its Annex I, which is the OECD text, and Directive 2001/83/EC applies GLP to non-clinical tests of medicines.

In the United States, the FDA's [21 CFR Part 58](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/58.1) applies to nonclinical laboratory studies supporting applications for research or marketing permits for FDA-regulated products, including human and animal drugs, medical devices, biological products and food and color additives. Part 58 defines a nonclinical laboratory study as in vivo or in vitro experiments in which test articles are studied prospectively under laboratory conditions to determine their safety; basic exploratory studies are excluded. The rule text quoted here is current as at November 2026.

GLP is distinct from manufacturing GMP. A contract research organization may need to meet both if it also performs GMP release testing, but the personnel records serve different purposes: GLP records support the integrity of a specific study, while GMP records support each batch. For manufacturing, see [EU GMP Chapter 2](/regulations/eu-gmp-chapter-2-personnel-training-requirements).

sections.heading: What does 21 CFR 58.29 require for personnel?

blocks.text: Section 58.29 requires qualified personnel and a current record of each person's training, experience and job description. The key text of [21 CFR 58.29](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/58.29) reads:

blocks.title: 21 CFR 58.29(a) and (b)
blocks.text: "(a) Each individual engaged in the conduct of or responsible for the supervision of a nonclinical laboratory study shall have education, training, and experience, or combination thereof, to enable that individual to perform the assigned functions. (b) Each testing facility shall maintain a current summary of training and experience and job description for each individual engaged in or supervising the conduct of a nonclinical laboratory study."

The rest of the section requires sufficient personnel to conduct the study according to protocol (58.29(c)), sanitation and health precautions, appropriate clothing, and exclusion of anyone with an illness that may affect study integrity, with all personnel instructed to report such conditions to their supervisor (58.29(d) to (f)).

items: **Testing facility management ([58.31](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/58.31)):** must assure that "personnel clearly understand the functions they are to perform" and that personnel and resources are available as scheduled.

**Study director ([58.33](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/58.33)):** a scientist or other professional of appropriate education, training and experience, who is the single point of study control.

**Quality assurance unit ([58.35](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/58.35)):** monitors each study to assure management that facilities, equipment, personnel, methods, practices, records and controls conform to Part 58, and must be entirely separate from and independent of the personnel conducting that study.

sections.heading: What do the OECD Principles of GLP require for training?

blocks.text: The OECD Principles put training records and role clarity among management's minimum responsibilities and require all study staff to know the GLP parts that apply to them. Section II.1.1(2) of the Principles, as reproduced in Annex I of Directive 2004/10/EC, says management should at a minimum:

items: "(c) ensure the maintenance of a record of the qualifications, training, experience and job description for each professional and technical individual;"
"(d) ensure that personnel clearly understand the functions they are to perform and, where necessary, provide training for these functions;"
"(g) ensure that for each study an individual with the appropriate qualifications, training, and experience is designated by the management as the study director before the study is initiated";
(h) for multisite studies, designate where needed a principal investigator who is appropriately trained, qualified and experienced to supervise the delegated phases.

blocks.text: Section II.1.4 adds a duty on the individual: "All personnel involved in the conduct of the study must be knowledgeable in those parts of the principles of good laboratory practice which are applicable to their involvement in the study." Study personnel must have access to the study plan and relevant standard operating procedures, comply with them, document deviations, and record raw data promptly and accurately. Quality assurance personnel must be designated by and directly responsible to management, familiar with the test procedures, and not involved in the study being assured (II.2.1).

sections.heading: How long must GLP training records be kept?

blocks.text: Training records are archived with the study records and kept for the regulatory retention period. Under [21 CFR 58.195](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/58.195), summaries of training and experience and job descriptions may be retained with other employment records for the periods in 58.195(a) and (b).

blocks.text: The OECD Principles (section II.10.1(c)) list "records of qualifications, training, experience and job descriptions of personnel" among materials retained in the archives for the period specified by the appropriate authorities, alongside quality assurance inspection records, master schedules and computerized system validation documentation. Only personnel authorized by management may access the archives. If a US testing facility goes out of business, its records transfer to the sponsor's archives and FDA must be notified in writing (58.195(h)).

sections.heading: Is the US GLP rule changing?

blocks.text: A revision was proposed in 2016 but has not been finalized. FDA published a [proposed rule on Good Laboratory Practice for Nonclinical Laboratory Studies](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2016/08/24/2016-19875/good-laboratory-practice-for-nonclinical-laboratory-studies) (81 FR 58342) on August 24, 2016, with comments due by November 22, 2016.

blocks.title: Proposed: not in force as at November 2026
blocks.text: Proposed 58.29(a) would add that qualifications "must include training and experience with GLP requirements" and that "Personnel who work with animals must have both general and species-specific training and experience." Proposed 58.29(d) would require any person conducting a phase of a study to keep a current summary of training and experience and a job description for each individual it employs on that phase, which matters for multisite studies. A Federal Register search in November 2026 found no final rule, and the eCFR text of 58.29 is unchanged.

Facilities can already document GLP-specific and species-specific training, since the OECD Principles expect personnel to know the GLP parts relevant to their role. Doing so makes the records ready for the proposal if it is finalized.

blocks.text: Linking each person's records to the specific SOP versions used in a study is easier with a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) built around [standard operating procedures](/glossary/standard-operating-procedure). See also [how to convert SOPs into training](/guides/how-to-convert-sops-into-training).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each SOP and technique to the study roles that use it and to the assessment that shows competence, so a facility can show which version each person was trained on at the time of a given study. The same approach supports [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences) research organizations.

faqs.a: Neither 21 CFR Part 58 nor the OECD Principles set an annual frequency. They require personnel to have the training needed for their assigned functions and management to provide training where necessary. Facilities set refresher intervals themselves, typically triggered by SOP revisions and periodic GLP updates.

faqs.q: Do GLP training records need to be signed by the trainee?
faqs.a: The rules do not prescribe signatures. They require a current summary of training and experience and a job description. Many facilities use trainee and trainer sign-off because it gives inspectors clear evidence of when training occurred and who verified it; electronic records must meet 21 CFR Part 11 in the US.

faqs.q: Does GLP training apply to exploratory or discovery research?
faqs.a: Not under the US rule. 21 CFR 58.3(d) excludes basic exploratory studies carried out to determine whether a test article has any potential utility, and studies using human subjects or clinical studies. GLP training and record duties attach to personnel working on nonclinical safety studies intended to support a regulatory submission.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for GLP training at a test facility?
faqs.a: Test facility management. The OECD Principles require management to maintain training records and provide training where necessary, and 21 CFR 58.31 requires management to assure that personnel clearly understand their functions. The study director ensures GLP compliance within each study, and QA monitors compliance independently.
